previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with a 5-day history of diffuse abdominal pain and low-grade fever following a recent hospitalization for catheter dislodgement and febrile neutropenia. Physical exam revealed rebound tenderness, and CT imaging showed colonic wall thickening at the hepatic flexure suggestive of non-specific colitis. He was initially treated with intravenous vancomycin and levofloxacin due to concern for infection in the setting of low white count. His symptoms improved, ANC remained above 1000, and he was transitioned to oral ciprofloxacin and metronidazole. A new left lower lobe opacity on chest X-ray was noted but remained asymptomatic. He was discharged home with instructions to complete antibiotics, resume lactulose, and follow up for kidney ultrasound and transplant evaluation. Blood and stool cultures remained pending at discharge.

radiology_notes.text:
PA AND LATERAL VIEWS OF THE CHEST

REASON FOR EXAM:  Fever.

Cardiac size is top normal.  Irregular consolidation in the left lower lobe is
consistent with pneumonia. right central catheter tip is in the cavoatrial
junction.  There is no pneumothorax or pleural effusion.  Enlargement of the
hila bilaterally is due to lymphadenopathy.

IMPRESSION:  Left lower lobe pneumonia and hilar lymphadenopathy.

Findings were discussed with Dr. ___ by phone on ___ at 11:21 a.m.,
5 minutes after the discovery of the findings.

ABDOMINAL ULTRASOUND AND LIVER DOPPLER

CLINICAL INDICATION:  Hep C cirrhosis with abdominal pain and low-grade
fevers, concern for possible SBP and to assess for portal vein patency.

The liver is coarse and echogenic throughout, but no focal liver lesions are
identified.  There is a trace ascites around the liver and spleen and a tiny
pocket is seen in the right lower quadrant, but there is insufficient volume
for safe paracentesis.  Spleen is again seen to be markedly enlarged and there
are extensive varices seen throughout the abdomen and notably in the
epigastrium, upper left retroperitoneum and in the splenic region.

Color flow and pulse Doppler waveforms were performed confirming the presence
of extensive varices.  The portal vein is patent, both in the main portal vein
and in the left and right branches, with low velocity forward flow.  Right
middle and left hepatic veins are also patent as well as the hepatic arteries
which show normal forms.  Limited views of the right and left kidneys show no
hydronephrosis.  The splenic vein and inferior vena cava are seen to be
patent, but the superior mesenteric vein cannot be well visualized due to gas.

CONCLUSION:  Study shows findings consistent with cirrhosis and portal
hypertension with extensive varices.  There is no focal liver lesion seen.

Only trace ascites is seen, insufficient for paracentesis at this time.
